scope: Proposition 5.1 (Orientation) of the manuscript “Randomized quasipolynomial-time mean-payoff games” (preprints/Randomized-quasipolynomial-time-mean-payoff-games-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 104 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4ab7552f58266134), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the lower-rank comparison guarantees stated at the beginning of this section. On a fixed permitted input (a, b; B, α, β, k, m) of rank r, let (χ, H) be the output of Orient. For every fixed admissible subsolution y of [a, b] whose core in Equation (5.1) satisfies α(Iy) > ηk, Pr (χ = Y or ∃H ∈ H : α(Sy ∩ H) > ηk) ≥ 1 − 1 16 . (5.2) Separately, for every fixed admissible supersolution z of [a, b] with β(Iz) > ηm, Pr (χ = Z or ∃H ∈ H : β(Sz ∩ H) > ηm) ≥ 1 − 1 16 . (5.3) On every tape, every set in H has µ-measure at most 1/2. Each probability statement remains valid conditional on a pre-call history that fixes its input and qualifying comparison, when the call uses fresh random bits.
